name: confounded_observational
query: does coffee raise the risk score
note: Synthetic data with a known data-generating process: smoking confounds the coffee/risk comparison, and the aggregate direction reverses inside the smoking strata (Simpson's paradox). The attempted write claims causal=verified while the identification assumption is still untested, so the gate must refuse it.

attempt.title: Coffee raises the synthetic risk score
attempt.body:
Synthetic cohort (n=4000, generated, not observed people).

| group | n | mean risk score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| coffee | 2000 | 6.1 |
| no coffee | 2000 | 5.2 |

Stratified by smoking, the direction reverses: coffee drinkers score lower in both strata. The aggregate difference is produced by smoking, which is associated with both coffee and risk.

causal_record.temporal_order: coffee habit recorded before the score
